dea-med-013.text: No. Amazon Redshift, a table FATO giant is often united (JOIN) to a table by a client_id column, and the queries suffer with redistribution of data between us. Which distribution style minimizes this shuffle?
options: DISTSTYLE KEY in both tables, using client_id as the distribution key
DISTSTYLE EVEN in the two tables
DISTSTYLE ALL in the table fact
dea-med-013.explanation: A) Correct: KEY the MESMA join column, the corresponding lines are in the same node (co-location) and the JOIN B) Incorrect: EVEN randomly spreads, ensuring the shuffle no JOIN. C) Incorrect: ALL copy the entire table in each node — unfeasible for giant fact tables. D) Incorrect: 'deactivate the AUTO' is not a strategy.

dea-med-014.text: What is the correct use of DISTSTYLE ALL no Redshift?
options: Tables made with billions of lines
Small and little modified DIMENSION Tables, fully copied for all nodes to accelerate JOINS
dea-med-014.explanation: A) Incorrect: replicate billions of lines in each node explodes storage. B) Incorrect: each writing replicates in all nodes — bad for intense writing. C) Incorrect: staging does not need replication. D) Correct: small dimensions (e.g. product table) in ALL are local to any JOIN, eliminating redistribution — the replicated storage cost is irrelevant to small tables.

dea-med-015.text: IB Dashboards no Redshift They're slow. APENAS on Monday mornings, when hundreds of analysts consult simultaneously. The cluster attends well the rest of the week and the team does not want to pay for a larger cluster all the time.?
options: Competition Scaling, adding automatic transitory clusters at peaks of competition
dea-med-015.explanation: A) Incorrect: restart does not add competition capacity.: RDS It's OLTP, no BI.D warehouse correct: the Competition Scaling adds automatic transitory capacity during peaks of simultaneous queries and removes it afterwards (with free daily credits).

dea-med-016.text: A precise start-up of data warehouse for ESPORADIC and unpredictable loads (a few hours a week), without managing cluster, paying only for the processing consumed. Redshift answer?
options: Cluster provided ra3 with reserve of 3 years
Amazon Redshift Serverless, charged by RPU-time during use
dea-med-016.explanation: A) Incorrect: 24/7 for a few hours per week is the opposite of efficient. B) Incorrect: booking of 3 years for sporadic use waste money. C) Incorrect: Spectrum is query extension to S3 — presupposes a warehouse/endpoint Redshift. D) Correct: Serverless automatically size and charge only while there are queries — perfect for intermittent use.

dea-med-017.text: A recurring consultation of the Athena Scan 2 TB of JSON raw to generate the same aggregate cut. MATERIALIZAR this result in S3 in Parquet partitioned, using the own Athena. Which resource to use?
options: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT (CTAS), defining Parquet format and partitioning in creation
dea-med-017.explanation: A) Incorrect: UNLOAD is from Redshift, (b) Incorrect: VACUUM is table maintenance (Redshift/Iceberg), non-materialization.: DynamoDB does not participate in this flow. CTAS executes the query and saves the result as a new table in S3, already in Parquet/compressed/shared — the following queries read the optimized dataset.

dea-med-018.text: The data team wants to impose a LIMITE of data scanned by reference to Athena to contain costs per team, in addition to separating the metrics of use of the marketing and financial team. Athena implements this?
options: Workgroups, with scanned and metric bytes limits per group
dea-med-018.explanation: A) Incorrect: Request Country transfers the cost of S3 to the applicant, does not limit queries. B) Incorrect: timeout does not control cost by bytes. C) Correct: workgroups isolate times, define location of results, apply data limits scanned by query (cancelling who exceeds) and publish separate metrics. D) Incorrect: Federated Query consults other sources — nothing to do with limits..

dea-med-019.text: A table of the DynamoDB needs to be analyzed with SQL complex with data lake data, SEM consumption of table reading capacity in production. What native approach attends?
options: Use native export of DynamoDB for the S3 (from PITR, without consuming RCUs) and consult with Athena
Rolling massive scans directly into the table
Transform the table into Global Table
dea-med-019.explanation: A) Correct: or export to S3 use continuous backup (PITR) — zero impact on the table — and the result (DynamoDB JSON/Ion) can be consulted via Athena. B) Incorrect: Massive scan consumes RCUs and threatens production. C) Incorrect: Global Tables are multi-region replication, not analysis. D) Incorrect: DynamoDB has no 'read replicas' as RDS.

dea-med-020.text: Repeative dashboard queries perform heavy aggregations always equal in Redshift. The team wants to pre-compute these results DENTRO warehouse, with managed update. Which resource to use?
options: Materialized Views, with REFRESH incremental when possible
dea-med-020.explanation: A) Incorrect: spreadsheets outside the warehouse break governance and do not scale. B) Incorrect: more we are brute force expensive for a calculation repetition problem. C) Correct: materialized views store the pre-computed result and can be updated incrementally — dashboards start reading the result ready. D) Incorrect: common views re-execute the entire query to each access.

dea-med-021.text: When comparing Apache Avro and Apache Parquet in a pipeline, what is the correct positioning of each format?
options: Both are compression formats, not file formats
Avro is columnar and Parquet is line to line
Parquet is always superior in all cases
Avro (based on LINHAS, with built-in schema) is strong for transport/streaming and schema evolution; Parquet (COLUNAR) is strong for analytical storage and queries
dea-med-021.explanation: A) Incorrect: they are formats of ARQUIVO/serialization; compression (Snappy), GZIP) is orthogonal. B) Incorrect: it is the reverse. C) Incorrect: for transport record record, Avro usually is better. D) Correct: this is the classic division — Avro serializes complete records (good for Kafka/Kinesis and schema contracts); Parquet organizes by columns (good for Athena/Spectrum/Spark analytical).

dea-med-022.text: A consultation at the Redshift almost always filter by date_sale. Scans are reading too many blocks. Which choice of physical design reduces the blocks read in this pattern?
options: Set Date_Sale as SORT KEY Table
dea-med-022.explanation: A) Incorrect: ALL is a small table replication, not related to the filter.: DISTKEY decides ONDE the lines stay (co-location of JOIN), (c) Incorrect: Redshift does not use B-tree indices as OLTP. D) Correct: with key sort on date_sale, the data is sorted on disk and zone metadata allows PULAR blocks outside the filter (zone maps) — minus I/O.

dea-med-023.text: A pipeline step in the Step Functions call one API unstable external. The team wants 3 new attempts with increasing interval and, if all fail, divert to a state of treatment that reports the team — TUDO without writing control code.?
options: Retry Blocks (with BackoffRate and MaxAttempts) and Catch in the very state of the machine
A cron that re-executes the entire pipeline
dea-med-023.explanation: (a) Incorrect: Lambda is fragile and reinvents what the platform gives ready. B) Incorrect: major timeout does not create retentatives. C) Correct: Retry/Catch are declarative in ASL: ErrorEquals, IntervalSeconds, BackoffRate, MaxAttempts and diversion to failback states. D) Incorrect: re-execute everything because of a wasteful step and does not isolate the error.

dea-med-024.text: A flow composed of components of the Glue (crawler → cleaning job → aggregation job) needs to be chained with conditional triggers (just follow if the previous step was successful). What option keeps the orchestration DENTRO of its own Glue?
options: Call jobs manually by the console
dea-med-024.explanation: A) Incorrect: manual operation is not orchestration.: Glue Workflows chain crawlers and jobs with triggers (scheduled, on demand, successful/failure) and graphical view of execution — no extra service. C) Incorrect: MWAA works, but adds an external orchestrator to a flow 100% Glue. D) Incorrect: AWS Backup is backup, not orchestration.
